note: No concept name, expected relation, or evaluation key appears anywhere in this file. The human's own words only, in English. Grammatical connectives are ordinary English; no architectural relation vocabulary is used as a label. Structural punctuation from other scripts is permitted but no other-script vocabulary is used.

teaching_examples.text: The alcove is set back from the passage because a person who is tired needs to recover away from the movement.
A niche sits apart from the corridor so that someone who is weary can recover quietly.
A bay stands back from the walkway for a visitor who is exhausted to recover in a still corner.
The bench is drawn away from the thoroughfare because a resting person needs to recover undisturbed.
The recess is pulled away from the busy lane so that a person who is unwell can recover in peace.
The hall opens onto the courtyard because the room needs to be entered easily.
The stair meets the landing because a walker needs to arrive somewhere clear.

filler_substituted_examples.text: The burrow is set back from the channel because a person who is tired needs to recover away from the movement.
A grotto sits apart from the gutter so that someone who is weary can recover quietly.
A cove stands back from the ditch for a visitor who is exhausted to recover in a still corner.
The stool is drawn away from the byway because a resting person needs to recover undisturbed.
The recess is pulled away from the noisy track so that a person who is unwell can recover in peace.

reformulated_examples.text: Because a person who is tired needs to recover away from the movement, the alcove is set back from the passage.
So that someone who is weary can recover quietly, a niche sits apart from the corridor.
In order that a visitor who is exhausted recovers in a still corner, a bay stands back from the walkway.

why_swapped_examples.text: The alcove is set back from the passage because the paint is a warm shade.
A niche sits apart from the corridor so that the plan is easier to draw.
A bay stands back from the walkway for the budget to stay the same.

counterfactual_examples.text: The alcove is set within the passage because a person who is tired needs to recover away from the movement.
A niche sits apart from the corridor so that someone who is weary can recover quietly.

novel_concept_corpus.note: N1 and N2 state a teaching relation using NO word from the predefined relation or scope vocabulary. They exist to test whether a novel relational pattern can be reached at all. They are NOT promised to succeed.

novel_teaching_examples.text: The bench turns its back on the plaza because a person who is reading needs to not be seen.
The seat turns its back on the street because someone who is thinking needs to not be seen.

novel_unseen_cases.text: The ledge turns its back on the road because a person who is resting needs to not be seen.

mode_p_probe_corpus.note: A SEPARATE, deliberately favourable corpus for the Mode-P baseline. In this corpus the humans' WHY literally contains the same word the predefined vocabulary supplies as a kind. It exists so the Mode-P baseline can be shown to reach its ceiling when, and only when, the reason happens to repeat the supplied vocabulary. This is the degenerate case that makes representation dependence measurable.

teaching_examples.text: The hall opens onto the court because access is needed for visitors.
The lobby opens onto the yard because access is needed for guests.
The room opens onto the garden because access is needed for people.

unseen_cases.text: The porch opens onto the lane because access is needed for walkers.
